title: Which central elements are transitive? An answer to a question of Campion Loth and Rattan on Jucys-Murphy evaluations
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. Transitive Jucys–Murphy images fill the centre of the symmetric group algebra exactly when (n−1)! is invertible, with optimal degree 2n−2.

Context. The symmetric group Sn consists of all rearrangements of n objects. The centre of its group algebra consists of the combinations of permutations that do not depend on how the objects are labelled; the class sums Kλ, each adding up all permutations of one cycle type, form a basis. The Jucys–Murphy elements Ji = (1 i) + … + (i−1 i) are sums of transpositions, and by theorems of Jucys and of Murphy the symmetric polynomials in them give exactly the centre, even over the integers. Expanding such a polynomial produces products of transpositions, whose counts are Hurwitz-type numbers. Keeping only the transitive products, those whose transpositions connect all n letters (connected branched covers), defines the transitive image Tn(f). Goulden and Jackson proved that transitive powers are central, and Campion Loth and Rattan proved that Tn(f) is central for every symmetric function f. They asked which subalgebra of the centre these transitive images generate (their Question 12).

Main results. (A) Over the complex numbers every central element is the transitive image of a single symmetric function, so the subalgebra asked for is the whole centre. Over an arbitrary commutative ring R, Tn is onto the centre if and only if (n−1)! is a unit in R, and the identity coefficients of transitive images form exactly the ideal (n−1)!R. (B) When (n−1)! is a unit, degree 2n−2 suffices, and the identity element is not the transitive image of any symmetric function of smaller degree. (C) The pairs (ordinary evaluation, transitive image) are exactly the pairs of central elements whose coefficients at the n-cycles agree. (D) Even the unital algebra generated by transitive images is the whole centre only when (n−1)! is a unit; for each prime p ≤ n−1 the class of a p-cycle stays out of reach modulo p. A conjugation-orbit argument shows that coefficients are divisible by zλ/hλ classwise. An exact, degree-free computation shows that this classwise bound describes the integral image exactly for n ≤ 5 and n = 7; for n = 6 the integral image has index 2 in the allowed lattice, cut out by one explicit parity condition; for every n ≤ 7 adding the scalars closes the image under multiplication.

Method. A Möbius inversion over set partitions writes Tn(f) as an alternating sum of ordinary evaluations on Jucys–Murphy elements of Young subgroups. Multiplying by the sum of the elements of a Young subgroup turns each Jucys–Murphy element into the number of smaller letters in its block, so suitable symmetric functions read off the block sizes and a triangular system can be inverted.

Limits. The paper answers Question 12 as posed. The description of the integral image is complete only for n ≤ 7, by exact computation, and the n = 6 parity condition has no conceptual explanation yet. Closed forms for transitive images of the classical bases (Question 13 of Campion Loth and Rattan) are not addressed.

Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF); verify_transitive.py, an exact standard-library Python verifier (marker construction and Möbius formula at word level, type selectors, the class-level engine against direct word expansion, the n = 3 matrix, the optimal degree, the pair rank, and the integral image for n ≤ 7); its recorded output; the bibliography; a machine-readable index; a research-gate record; a review summary; a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. All arithmetic is exact; every check exits with status 1 on failure, also under python -O.

Assurance. Written proofs with exact computational checks. Internal AI-assisted review only: a five-role Claude review panel run as one combined pass, the lead's proof audit and exact verifier with negative controls, one revision round with an extension, then a re-review and proof audit of the revised text. Jucys (1974) and Murphy (1983) were read in full. No second-model (Astra/Codex) review took place. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous.
